# Getting Started with HATSA

HATSA (Hyperalignment via Task-informed Shared Analysis) provides methods for aligning functional brain data across subjects, with optional task-informed variants. This guide shows the basic workflow and the main entry points.

## Installation

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Install from GitHub
devtools::install_github("bbuchsbaum/hatsa")
```

```{r setup}
library(hatsa)
```

## Your First Alignment

The simplest way to use HATSA is with the `hatsa()` function:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Assume you have a list of subject data matrices
# Each matrix is timepoints × parcels (or voxels)
result <- hatsa(subject_data)

# By default, HATSA:
# - Selects anchors automatically (MRA-based)
# - Uses a preset configuration (default/fast/accurate)
# - Returns a fitted `hatsa_projector`
```

## Understanding Your Results

HATSA provides simple functions to explore your results:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Get a quick summary
hatsa_summary(result)

# Extract aligned data
aligned_data <- get_aligned_data(result)

# Get the group template
template <- get_template(result)

# Visualize alignment quality
plot_hatsa(result, type = "eigenvalues")
```

## Choosing Parameters

Not sure what parameters to use? Let HATSA help:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Get suggestions based on your data
params <- hatsa_suggest(subject_data)

# Use the suggestions
result <- hatsa(subject_data, 
                components = params$components,
                preset = params$preset)
```

## Task-Informed Alignment

If you have task information, HATSA can use it to improve alignment:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# task_data is a list parallel to subject_data.
# Each task matrix should be either:
#   - C × V_p (features/conditions × parcels), or
#   - V_p × C (parcels × features)
#
# Automatic method selection + automatic anchors
result <- hatsa_task(subject_data, task_data, method = "auto")

# Or choose a specific method
result <- hatsa_task(subject_data, task_data, method = "blend", task_strength = "strong")

# More control: build a validated config and pass it to task_hatsa()
cfg <- hatsa_config(preset = "default", task_method = "lambda_blend", lambda_blend_value = 0.25)
result2 <- task_hatsa(subject_data_list = subject_data,
                      task_data_list = task_data,
                      anchor_indices = 1:min(50, ncol(subject_data[[1]])),
                      spectral_rank_k = 20,
                      task_method = "lambda_blend",
                      opts = cfg)
```

## Presets for Different Scenarios

HATSA includes presets optimized for different use cases:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Fast mode for exploration
result_fast <- hatsa(subject_data, preset = "fast")

# Accurate mode for final analyses  
result_accurate <- hatsa(subject_data, preset = "accurate")

# Default balanced mode
result_default <- hatsa(subject_data, preset = "default")
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Built-in documentation
?hatsa
?hatsa_task
?hatsa_config

# Parameter validation
hatsa_validate_params(subject_data, 
                      anchor_indices = my_anchors,
                      spectral_rank_k = 30)
```
